div.div:
مُعْتَتَبٌ [is used, agreeably with analogy, in the sense of the inf. n. of اِعْتَتَبَ]. El-Kumeyt says, “الشَّوْقُ مِنْ فُؤَادِى وَٱلش ↓ فٱعْتَتَبَ
شِعْرُ إِلَى مَنْ إِلَيْهِ مُعْتَتَبُ
” [And desire turned away from my heart, and my poetry unto him unto whom was its turning]. (S, O.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
